- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually underestimates later days.
- Strong bias toward higher prices in the first 10–15 days of the forecast, followed by sharp downward drift — suggests model fails to capture sudden market corrections or policy-driven price drops.
- Overshoot after spikes: when prices spike (e.g., 45.93 or 44.49), model forecasts a prolonged upward trend, then sharply drops — indicates failure to model volatility decay or market correction after peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after spikes, then undercorrect upward after dips — suggests model lacks dynamic adjustment to recent price momentum.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts show persistent underestimation of low-price periods (e.g., 34.33, 33.70) — model fails to recognize prolonged price suppression or regulatory intervention.
- Lagged response: model reacts slowly to recent price drops — e.g., 34.33 appears in forecast only after 10–15 days, suggesting delayed adjustment to market signals.
